findings.summary: Companion guide states a refuted fact: 'a forged commit-graph file (git validates it against the objects ...)'.
findings.detail: Reviewer built a diverged repo (c3 local, c2 remote, both children of c1), wrote a commit-graph and binary-patched c2's CDAT parent to c3 (checksum recomputed). git 2.53.0 then ACCEPTS the forged graph: `git log --format=%P -1 c2` prints c3 and `git rev-list --count c3..c2` = 1 (true value 2); with core.commitGraph=false log shows c1. `git merge-base --is-ancestor c3 c2` was NOT fooled in 4 variants (generation v1/v2, with/without date change) and the verifier still exits 12, so no false pass was demonstrated: the verdict path is UNCONFIRMED-safe, but the guide's stated reason is false (11.4.6). Also docs line 125 still lists 'a per-repository .git/info exclude' as uncovered, contradicting the R2 fix, and the Status row still says 'round 7 documentation sync'. Candidate fix: add `-c core.commitGraph=false` to $GIT (removes the class at negligible cost), correct both doc statements, add a forged-graph fixture as golden case.

findings.summary: R2 fix turns globally-ignored editor/OS files into exit 13, and the refusal names no file.
findings.detail: Clean repo + global core.excludesFile '*.swp .idea/' + .f.swp and .idea/ws.xml: verifier exit 13, dirty_untracked=2, stderr note gives a count only, the report contains no file name. Same with the XDG default ignore file (no core.excludesFile set): plain git status shows 0 lines, verifier exit 13. The fixer documents this consequence (guide line 161), so it is a stated policy, not a hidden bluff; but under 11.4.201(1) it is a refusal where git's own definition says clean, and 11.4.201(5) wants the resolved evidence on every refusal. Owner decision owed: keep (strict), or report hidden files in a separate field/list them on stderr and make them non-failing outside --strict. Impact on this repository today: 0 hidden files on this host.

findings.summary: `bash verify_repos.sh` (interpreter invocation) still sources a caller BASH_ENV in the entry process.
findings.detail: The `#!/bin/bash -p` shebang only applies to direct execution; BASH_ENV=<canary> bash verify_repos.sh ... ran the canary once (workers and the xargs dispatch are -p and clean). Either state 'execute directly, never via bash' in the header/guide, or add a guard (e.g. re-exec with `bash -p` when `$-` lacks p, or `[[ $- == *p* ]] || exec /bin/bash -p "$0" "$@"`). CPA runs use env -i, so impact is standalone runs only.
